input: MetadataSharp-authored deterministic 8x8 RGB bytes: pixel_data(seed) = bytes((i*17+seed)%256 for i in range(192)); no captures, external sample files, or third-party source/test bytes used. Metadata Artist B7Artist and CreatorTool B7Tool are authored for these probes.
recipe: tools/reference/b7_owned_fixtures.py encode_catalog; exact options and seeds are in the generator; SHA-256 and output lengths are in manifest.json. Binary fixture data are committed; normal offline tests validate those bytes rather than silently re-encoding them.
encodingEnvironment: Linux x86_64 CPython 3.11 manylinux wheels: Pillow 11.3.0 / libavif 1.3.0, pillow-heif 1.1.0 / libheif 1.20.1 / x265 4.1+1-1d117be, imagecodecs 2025.8.2 / libjxl 0.11.1, numpy 2.2.6. Encoder tools are external development tools, not product dependencies.
scope: AVIF/HEIF/HEIC probes have EXIF Artist and XMP CreatorTool. HEIF and HEIC are separate independently encoded HEVC stills, not distinct codec coverage: both use the HEIC brand. JXL probes are bare codestream and container. The container has authored EXIF and XMP boxes; the bare codestream has no metadata boxes. Neither has authored IPTC. No CR3 fixture has been generated.
observedDecoding: In the generation environment ImageMagick 6.9.11-60/libheif 1.15.1 displayed all three AVIF/HEIF/HEIC inputs as 8x8. JPEG XL encodings decoded to the authored 8x8 pixels using imagecodecs/libjxl, the same implementation that encoded them, so this is not an independent JXL oracle.
limitations: No independently verified full normative conformance, HEVC patent clearance, representative CR3, imported sample license, or general image-codec validity is claimed. HEVC-coded files have an ispe canvas of 64x64 with an 8x8 clean aperture: do not mistake raw canvas dimensions for display size. These are tiny black-box probes, not a comprehensive corpus.
